title: Duncker Streett & Co. Inc. Acquires 5,082 Shares of Apple (AAPL)
text:
Duncker Streett & Co. Inc. increased its holdings in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 11.7% in the fourth quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the SEC. The institutional investor owned 48,658 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after purchasing an additional 5,082 shares during the quarter. Apple accounts for 2.1% of Duncker Streett & Co. Inc.’s holdings, making the stock its 2nd biggest position. Duncker Streett & Co. Inc.’s holdings in Apple were worth $8,234,000 as of its most recent SEC filing. 
Other hedge funds and other institutional investors have also bought and sold shares of the company. FNY Managed Accounts LLC grew its stake in shares of Apple by 852.4% during the 2nd quarter. FNY Managed Accounts LLC now owns 800 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $115,000 after acquiring an additional 716 shares in the last quarter. Private Vista LLC bought a new position in shares of Apple during the 2nd quarter worth approximately $122,000. Crow Point Partners LLC grew its stake in shares of Apple by 100.0% during the 3rd quarter. Crow Point Partners LLC now owns 1,000 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $153,000 after acquiring an additional 500 shares in the last quarter. Oak Point Wealth Management bought a new position in shares of Apple during the 4th quarter worth approximately $163,000. Finally, Interactive Financial Advisors bought a new position in shares of Apple during the 4th quarter worth approximately $188,000. 61.35% of the stock is owned by institutional investors and hedge funds. 
In other news, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of Apple stock in a transaction dated Friday, April 13th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total transaction of $6,833,048.52. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 64,475 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $11,261,203.50. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through the SEC website . Also, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of Apple stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, April 4th. The shares were sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total value of $2,938,460.00. Following the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares in the company, valued at $11,194,221.92. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . In the last quarter, insiders sold 125,988 shares of company stock worth $21,336,201. Company insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock. Several brokerages have recently weighed in on AAPL. Nomura set a $175.00 price target on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research note on Tuesday, April 3rd. Vetr downgraded Apple from a “strong-buy” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $186.86 price objective for the company. in a report on Monday, April 2nd. BMO Capital Markets downgraded Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and increased their price objective for the company from $162.00 to $166.00 in a report on Wednesday, January 31st. Royal Bank of Canada set a $203.00 price objective on Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Tuesday, April 3rd. Finally, Morningstar set a $170.00 price objective on Apple and gave the company a “neutral” rating in a report on Friday, February 2nd. Two investment analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have given a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the stock. Apple presently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $203.21.
Apple stock opened at $172.80 on Friday. Apple has a 12-month low of $141.16 and a 12-month high of $183.50. The company has a current ratio of 1.24, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. The stock has a market capitalization of $904,392.13, a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.76, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.35 and a beta of 1.25. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $87.62 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the business posted $3.36 earnings per share. The business’s revenue for the quarter was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. equities analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.37 earnings per share for the current fiscal year. 
Apple Company Profile 
Apple Inc (Apple) designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and portable digital music players, and a variety of related software, services, peripherals, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. The Company’s products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple TV, a portfolio of consumer and professional software applications, the iOS and OS X operating systems, iCloud, and a variety of accessory, service and support offerings.
